cards.html: Monte Carlo Simulations teaches you to answer questions about uncertainty by playing them out many times on a computer: how to build a simulation, how many runs it needs, how to make it faster, when to use it, and above all what goes wrong. It starts from zero: school maths (averages, percentages, squares and square roots) and basic Python are enough for the first skills. Every new word is explained when it first appears, and each skill starts with a short "Key word" table.

The track is a ramp. Skills 1 to 3 build intuition with coins, dice and a commute. Skills 4 to 6 add the working tools: error bars, faster sampling and the classic mistakes. Skills 7 to 9 reach university level, with the related methods, real industry uses and a full case study. By the end you should be able to design, run, check and defend a simulation at work. Plan on a bit over an hour of reading, plus the exercises.

Key wordPlain meaning
Monte Carlo simulationAnswering a question by playing it out many times at random and averaging
RunOne random play-through
numpyThe Python library for fast arrays of numbers, used in every example

cards.s: How the tree is laid out
cards.html: The first skill is the core idea. The tree then splits: the left path is building the model, the right path is the random numbers that drive it. They join at "How many runs?". It splits again into making simulations efficient (left) and making them right (right), then into choosing methods and real uses, and ends with a capstone case study.

Symbol or termMeaning
Nnumber of simulation runs (trials)
x̂ or "estimate"the average (or other statistic) over the N runs
MCSEMonte Carlo standard error: the sampling error of the estimate
P50, P80the 50th and 80th percentiles of a simulated output
rnga numpy random generator from np.random.default_rng

Code is short numpy that you can paste and run (start each session with import numpy as np). Every number quoted in the text comes from running that code with the seed shown. Each skill ends with a self-check, and the answers are hidden behind a tap.
